title: GAP Waiver Addenda: Expiration and the Fully Earned Charge
content:
**Rule.** An active GAP Waiver Addendum expires on its expiration date, which is the contract's original maturity date. It expires on that date even when extensions have moved the contract's maturity later. From that day it covers no loss and is fully earned, so no refund is due. A contract that is still open after expiration simply has no GAP coverage for its remaining installments.

| Situation | Consequence |
|---|---|
| Loss on or before the expiration date while the addendum is active | the loss falls within the coverage period |
| Loss after the expiration date | no GAP coverage |
| Contract extended past its original maturity | the addendum still expires on the original maturity date |
| Cancellation request after expiration | no refund, because the charge is fully earned |

*Hypothetical case.* A contract signed for 60 months receives two one-month extensions, and its last installment now falls two months after the original maturity date. The addendum still expires on the original maturity date. The final two installments carry no GAP coverage.
